title: EAST tokamak long-pulse operation
summary: China's experimental tokamak, holder of the record for sustained high-confinement plasma.
bodyHtml:
What This Is

The Experimental Advanced Superconducting Tokamak in Hefei sustained high-confinement plasma for 1,066 seconds in January 2025, a duration record rather than a power record. A companion facility, the Burning Plasma Experimental Superconducting Tokamak, is under construction with a target of demonstrating energy gain around 2027. Long pulses matter because they test materials, heat exhaust and control, the engineering problems that stand between experiments and plants.

Status

Attribute Value
Development stage Proof of concept
Estimated window 2025–2035
Confidence label Confident
Evidence Editorial synthesis of company, agency and press reporting
Compiled 18 November 2026

Related records

  • China's 15th Five-Year Plan

Investment Exposure

Fusion timelines remain long, but China is now setting the pace on pulse duration, which is the least glamorous and most necessary metric.

What Would Change The View

  • BEST's first plasma and gain claims.
  • Divertor and material endurance.
  • Whether private Chinese fusion entrants emerge.

Record Notes

Editorial brief, not an imported source note. Named milestones are drawn from company, agency and press reporting; forward dates are announced targets, not verified outcomes. No figure here is an audited statistic.
